items.title: Building Frontier Models: PMs as Quality Arbiters
points: Tulsee Doshi, Google's Gemini head of product, says frontier AI model development requires balancing rigorous evals (systematic testing frameworks for measuring model performance) with qualitative judgment—neither alone suffices.
Development compared to 'Snape's potions class': precise engineering paired with intuitive artistry, since evals alone cannot measure subjective quality or emergent capabilities.
PMs conduct 'vibes checks' (subjective, qualitative assessment of model behavior) alongside formal metrics to detect subtle improvements competitors might miss.
Writing effective evals requires domain expertise: start with concrete test cases, define clear pass/fail criteria, then scale via expert crowdsourcing.

items.title: The 60-20-20 Shipping Framework
points: 60% of features/capabilities should be fully validated, proven technology ready for production.
20% reserved for near-certain features validated in testing but not yet shipped at scale, reducing technical debt from untested experiments.
20% kept for experimental, high-upside bets to allow innovation without destabilizing the core product.

items.title: Google's Multimodal, Full-Stack AI Strategy
points: Beyond Gemini (text/image model), Google runs Nano Banana (efficient lightweight model), Genie (world simulation model), Veo (video generation model), Lyria (audio model), and Gemini Audio for real-time conversational AI.
Full-stack approach—controlling model architecture, infrastructure, and user-facing apps—enables tighter feedback loops and faster iteration than pure API or licensing models.
Specialized models target specific domains (music, video, reasoning) rather than a one-size-fits-all approach, improving quality and efficiency.

items.title: Rising Importance of PM Skills in AI Labs
points: As research complexity grows, product leadership becomes a critical differentiator between what works in papers and what actually ships to users.
PMs bridge research teams, infrastructure engineers, and end-users, identifying which capabilities matter most and which evals best predict real-world success.

issues.subject:
What it actually takes to build frontier models | Tulsee Doshi (Head of
 Product for Gemini)

headlines: Tulsee Doshi, Google's Gemini head of product, discusses how frontier AI model development requires balancing rigorous evals (systematic testing frameworks) with qualitative judgment—neither alone suffices.

Google pursues a full-stack frontier AI strategy, building across language models, multimodal systems (audio, video, images), and specialized models like Genie (world simulation) and Veo (video generation).

PMs in frontier labs focus on evals, vibes-checking (subjective quality assessment), and shipping discipline—using Doshi's 60-20-20 framework: 60% proven capabilities, 20% new but reliable features, 20% experimental.

Writing effective evals requires domain expertise: start with concrete test cases, define pass/fail criteria clearly, then scale via expert crowdsourcing when needed.
